Song decoding remains unresolved. Note the search's null: 55 of 100 random 32-byte RAM windows also map to some on-disk file span, because overlay code is resident verbatim — any future RAM-to-file match must clear that bar, not merely exist.

Two live GameLink RAM captures read a nonzero segment at the exact mov [0x0012], cx cell (0x5f39 and 0x6173, differing between snapshots) against a universal on-disk default of 0x0000, which falsifies the alternative that ES lives only in registers with no stored word. STILL UNFOUND, and now as a MEASURED NEGATIVE rather than an unattempted question: the MIDI.DAX music-timeline buffer. Both captured buffers decode cleanly under the format grammar (11,090 events, 0 malformed, clean 0xFC termination each) but BOTH appear verbatim inside Champions of Krynn/SOUND.DAX block 1 -- they are SFX-bank installs through the same generic slot-1 mechanism, not music. No static candidate cleared both its x86-code-alias disqualifier and its score bar either: the paragraph self-reference predicate returned 1 hit in 3 of 4 dumps against a shuffled-dump null of 0, and every survivor was disqualified as ordinary code or scored below the null's own maximum. Two pre-existing measurement bugs were fixed before any of it: a null sampler that drew 938 of an intended 1000 windows, and a case-insensitive-filesystem double-glob that counted every CoK .DAX twice (sources 1,592 -> 814, windows 45,504 -> 25,271) and had corrupted round 32's own top-5 with literal duplicate entries. A plan-supplied formula is a hypothesis, not a constant. tools/mididax_song_locate.py, docs/midi-dax-format.md 1.8.

ROUND 34 R6 (2026-09-04) CORRECTS THE 'MEASURED NEGATIVE' DIRECTLY ABOVE, not just narrows it (docs/engine/research/cok-sound-bank.md): SOUND.DAX block 1 is not merely an SFX bank. Its own header's first word (0x007d = 125, not the round-33 report's manually chosen 128) is a genuine, driver-disassembly-confirmed stream-start pointer -- the SAME 'mov ax, es:[0]; mov [cell], ax' install-time idiom independently confirmed in both MIDI.DAX block 1 and block 3. Segmenting the 13,936-byte stream on control-change markers finds three long, balanced, multi-voice passages (1,141 / 4,801 / 5,132 events, 5 voices each, Note-On/Off balance 0.994-0.999; corpus-wide totals 5,538 Note-On == 5,538 Note-Off exactly) -- the shape of real music, not short one-shot SFX. Three independent live GameLink RAM captures kept from round 33 (no new DOSBox-X session run this round) show the resident AdLib driver's own persisted cursor cell (block 3's 0x340, correcting the block-1-specific 0x2b7 the round-33 doc under-specified as universal) landing inside the largest, 4,801-event segment at two different points in a real session (an 'SSI presents' splash and live demo gameplay), with the cursor value itself advancing between nominally-identical captures -- evidence of a live, advancing playback position, not a frozen artifact. Round 33's 'this is SFX, not a song' verdict answered a different question (is this the MISSING music-timeline buffer) than this round's (does this SAME buffer ALSO hold song-shaped content the driver visits during play) -- the buffer holds BOTH short SFX-shaped fragments and long song-shaped passages. NOT (yet) claimed: that a real 0x388 AdLib OUT instruction fires from this exact code path during these specific captures -- block 3's static AdLib identity (port 0x388) was established in an earlier round from the driver's own disassembly, not re-verified against a live OUT trace this round, so audible hardware output remains inferred from driver identity, not directly observed this round. packages/engine/src/audio/dosSong.ts ports the decoder/segmenter to TypeScript (11/11 tests) but is NOT wired into apps/web/src/audio/gameAudio.ts as of this item (Phase B).

ROUND 35 R2 (2026-09-05) CORRECTS THE EVENT-FRAMING NUMBERS IN THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE: the event record is THREE bytes (2 data bytes + 1 trailing wait byte for 0x90/0x80 note events, 1 + 1 for 0xC0 program changes), measured from the driver's own code, not one. tools/mididax_event_frame.py derives each MIDI.DAX block's interpreter entry from its own slot-0 stub, disassembles it (capstone) and counts SI advancement per dispatch branch; blocks 1 (C/MS), 3 (AdLib), 4 (Tandy) and 5 (PC speaker) agree exactly, and block 2 (MPU-401) uses MIDI's own widths for 0xB0/0xD0/0xC0 plus the same trailing wait byte. This gap previously read that the Amiga single-bank wall-brick reassembly was EXHAUSTED and rejected — 96 hypotheses swept, plus a second blocker that the chunks' own palette is all-zero so no reassembly could be coloured. That was a TOOL BUG, not a property of the data: the sweep read the DOS bank with an 8-byte tile-STRIP parser when DoK's 256-tile banks are a 17-byte tile-ARRAY, so correct Amiga tiles were scored against garbage. Scope of that win, stated plainly: this is the SAME art DOS has, read from Amiga bytes. The toggle became truthful for DoK's walls; it did not make them richer. Six tiles (7 pixels, all in tile 255's bottom row) still differ.

ecl.detail: Round 31 built a dispatch map from Matrix Cubed's OWN GAME.OVR (tools/map_matrix_ecl_dispatch.py) and shipped the result as ECL_GEN1_MATRIX in packages/engine/src/ecl/disassemble.ts, wired to the ?ecl=matrix inspector route. The starting point remains true and is why this is not a copy of Countdown's entry: Matrix's GAME.OVR carries FBOV -- Curse of the Azure Bonds' overlay magic -- not Countdown's TPOV, so nothing was assumed to carry over. The dispatcher and operand parser were located by the same structural match against the CoAB oracle that Countdown's own tool uses (dispatcher similarity 0.8885/trigram 0.6087; operand parser 0.8750/0.9059). Header shape was read from Matrix's own ECL1.DAX bytes, not inherited: all 33 blocks open with the 0x1388 magic and put the fifth far pointer's vaddr at 0x8014, giving headerLen 22 / vbase 0x7ffe. Matrix dispatches the same 75 opcodes as Countdown with an identical measured word set and 0 disagreements. How much of that agreement is DISCRIMINATING was computed after an adversarial pass attacked the original wording, which said '53 agreeing on a concrete value, 22 both-unmeasured, 0 disagreements' without naming the alternative: the alternative is 'Matrix follows the plain Gen1/CoAB base table', and on most opcodes Countdown's dialect never diverged from that base, so agreeing there costs the alternative nothing. The real arm is 16 of 75, not 53 -- 8 opcodes where the effective word set differs from the base table AND Matrix's own handler yields a concrete value (0x0c, 0x1d, 0x22, 0x23, 0x27, 0x31, 0x3f, 0x40, including 0x27 jumping from base 8 to 2), plus the 8 beyond-0x40 extension opcodes with a measured width, for which the base table has no row at all. Matrix matches Countdown on 16 of 16. 56 shared-range opcodes carry the same word set under plain Gen1 as under ECL_GEN1_MATRIX and so separate nothing, and 22 are vacuous because neither handler reaches the parser. 0x3c is the instructive near-miss: Buck overrides it (base 1 -> 0) so it looks discriminating, but Matrix's own handler is no_far_call and measured nothing, which is why the arm is 8 and not 9. packages/engine/test/matrixEclDialect.test.ts computes this partition rather than restating it. Also 0x2b/0x31 share one compiled handler at offset 0x1c99 in Matrix's binary too, the code-identity evidence Countdown's SHORT_MENU override rests on. Against the corpus, 29 of the 33 retail blocks reach a clean terminating EXIT and 4 desync (blocks 1, 18, 20, 24) -- but that census is NOT the evidence and must not be read as it. Plain Gen1 scores 26/7 on the same blocks, and ECL_GEN1_SHORT_POOLS, a dialect that is wrong for Matrix, ties at exactly 29/4. A raw clean-exit count does not discriminate here; the binary does. WHY THIS IS 'partial' AND NOT 'supported': the derived table came back field-for-field equal to ECL_GEN1_BUCK, so the corpus census under the two dialects is identical BY CONSTRUCTION, not because it was measured twice -- that agreement is arithmetic and is evidence about the two dispatchers, not about these blocks. The eleven beyond-0x40 extension opcodes keep uncertain:true here for the same reason they do in Countdown: their word set was read from a handler prefetch, their MEANING never was. ECL_GEN1_MATRIX is a separate literal rather than an alias precisely so the deep-equal pin in packages/engine/test/matrixEclDialect.test.ts stays able to fail.
gaps: 3 of the 33 retail ECL blocks still desync under ECL_GEN1_MATRIX (blocks 18@0x14b0, 20@0x2f2, 24@0x26c) -- the same unresolved class as Countdown's own remaining two. That is a site this patch REVEALS rather than fixes, and counting it as progress would be counting the same block twice. Blocks 20 and 24 are untouched and unrelated to the three opcodes.
